hypotheses.justification: Lean adds this as an argument automatically: it is instance-implicit and 𝒪 is already an argument. Nothing in the statement or the proof needs it. `opFamily`, `heckeTL` and `diamondL` (Definitions/Def_CohCarrier_Inst.lean) only need `[CommRing 𝒪]` and `[NeZero M]`. `diamondL_top_eq_one` (line 171 of the same file) only needs `[CommRing 𝒪] [NeZero M]`. `CohCarrier.heckeT_comm_of_prime` works for any `AddCommGroup V`, with no condition on 𝒪. `Nat.coprime_primes` is about ℕ only. So `omit [IsDomain 𝒪] in` leaves the proof valid unchanged.

Same as for `[IsDomain 𝒪]`: Lean adds it automatically because 𝒪 is an argument, but it appears nowhere in the statement. Every lemma and definition the proof uses (`opFamily`, `heckeTL`, `diamondL_top_eq_one`, `heckeT_comm_of_prime`, `Nat.coprime_primes`) needs at most `[CommRing 𝒪]`. The proof is unchanged without it.

Same as for `[IsDomain 𝒪]`: Lean adds it automatically because 𝒪 is an argument, but nothing uses it. The commutation follows from `heckeT_comm_of_prime`, which holds for any `AddCommGroup V`, and from `diamondL_top_eq_one`, which only needs `[CommRing 𝒪] [NeZero M]`. The proof is unchanged without it.
